newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's MTRC cruises to 28 pct profit rise in 1996.
newsitem.headline: HK's MTRC cruises to 28 pct profit rise in 1996.

text.p: Hong Kong's Mass Transit Railway Corp (MTRC) said on Thursday that growth in passenger throughput and takings from tickets in 1996 boosted its net profits by more than 28 percent.
"In 1996, our passenger ridership has grown by 0.5 percent to 817 million and fare revenue increased to HK$5,078 million," chairman Jack So said in a statement.
With operating costs well-contained, net profit hit HK$1,535 million, up 28.3 percent compared with HK$1,196 million in 1995, the statement said.

It was the first time the company, a government-owned autonomous corporation that has the right to raise its own funds, was able to show a retained profit, allowing it to declare a dividend of HK$647 million.
"The corporation's brought-forward accumulated losses were extinguished during the year, and there is a retained profit for the first time since the railway commenced operation in 1979."

The company said its financial position had been boosted in the year by an injection of HK$8 billion in equity capital by the government under the provision of the Airport Railway Financial Support Agreement.
Hong Kong's existing subway network will eventually link up with an airport railway line, which will ferry passengers to and from the territory's new airport at Chek Lap Kok.
The MTRC added significant progress had been made in the construction of the airport railway.
"The corporation remains confident that the railway will be opened on time and within budget in the second quarter of 1998."

The company also made reference to instances of train delays in 1996, which sparked fierce criticism by passengers and the local media, forcing it at one point to import a transport consultant to help sort out the problems.
"We continue to undertake a substantial amount of capital and revenue works every year to maintain and enhance the operating railway system," it said.
